topic: Claude Opus 5.5 in plain words: what changed, how it compares with Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, when to use which, how to ask it to check its own work, and how to switch
audience: Professionals who use Claude at work and want to know whether to change model, without reading benchmark tables
goal: Pick the right model and effort for each job, switch in the model menu, and add a self-check step to important work
notes: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22, 2026 as the first model in the Claude 5.5 family. Anthropic says it performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]
Anthropic says Opus 5.5 generates output more than 30% faster than Opus 5 and, at default settings, costs 40% less on typical workloads. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]
Opus 5.5 API pricing is $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, 20% less than Opus 5. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

Anthropic says Opus 5.5 communicates more naturally: clearer writing, the most important information up front, less jargon, and it follows the writing rules you give it. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]
Anthropic writes: 'In our own use, this has made Opus 5.5's work easier to follow and check.' [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

In an internal Anthropic test, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Opus 5 wrote a report on a company's quarterly performance from a copy of the web; an automated grader checked every figure and quote against sources. Across effort settings, 16 of 18 Opus 5.5 reports cleared the bar, where any invented figure or quote failed. Neither Fable 5.1 nor Opus 5 cleared it in any attempt. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

An early tester quoted on Anthropic's announcement says Opus 5.5 'checks its own work in creative ways' and that 'self-verification loops feel easier to set up'. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

Anthropic-reported knowledge-work benchmark GDPval-AA v2.1 (real-world work across 44 occupations): Opus 5.5 1846 Elo, Fable 5.1 1735, Opus 5 1708. Terminal-Bench 4.0: Opus 5.5 66.4%, Opus 5 52.3%. Results use max effort (Terminal-Bench at xhigh) with production safeguards on. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

Anthropic says benchmark margins have become a less reliable guide to real-world differences, and that in its own use the gap between Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 is narrower than the scores suggest. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

Examples Anthropic cites: one tester completed a 680,000-line code migration in under a day, and Opus 5.5 succeeded 39 of 40 times at cutting web-app load times. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

With the Opus 5.5 launch, Anthropic raised five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans and gave subscribers a rate limit reset to use when they choose. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

The current lineup: Claude Fable 5.2 (demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work), Opus 5.5 (long-running agentic coding and knowledge work), Sonnet 5.5 (best combination of speed and intelligence) and Haiku 5.5 (high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks). Anthropic's docs advise starting with Opus 5.5 if unsure. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview]

Anthropic recommends starting most coding and knowledge tasks with Opus 5.5 as the 'strongest daily driver', moving up to Fable or down to Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5 as needed. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2]
Comparative latency: Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 'Moderate', Sonnet 5.5 'Fast', Haiku 5.5 'Fastest'. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview]
API list prices per million tokens (input/output): Fable 5.2 $8/$40, Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Haiku 5.5 from $0.10/$0.50. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview]
Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 each have a 1M-token context window, 128K max output and a June 2026 reliable knowledge cutoff. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview]
Training-data cutoffs: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 to June 2026; Opus 5 to May 2026. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114494-how-up-to-date-is-claude-s-training-data]

In chat on paid plans, Opus 5.5 and Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 have 1M-token context windows. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans]

Claude Sonnet 5.5 was announced September 28, 2026 as the second Claude 5.5 model: an upgrade over Sonnet 5 that runs 30%+ faster and costs up to 30% less for most work, at $2/$10 per million tokens. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5]

Anthropic positions Sonnet 5.5 as strongest at well-scoped everyday tasks, fixing bugs, and creating polished documents, slides and spreadsheets, while Opus 5.5 is for complex work needing careful judgment. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5]
In Claude Code and the Claude apps the default effort is Medium, while the Claude Platform (API) defaults to High. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5]

Claude Haiku 5.5 was announced October 7, 2026 as Anthropic's cheapest, fastest and most capable small model, built for high-volume work, and the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5]
On the Free plan the pricing table shows Sonnet and Haiku as available, but not Opus or Fable; Opus is available on Pro, Max and Ultra. [https://claude.com/pricing]

Claude Sonnet 4.6 leaves the model selector on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra on December 8, 2026, with Sonnet 5.5 recommended as the replacement. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/18537562-claude-sonnet-4-6-is-leaving-the-model-selector]

The selected model is shown below the text input on web and desktop and at the top of the screen on mobile; clicking it opens the model selector. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude]

To change the model, click the model name next to the send button and pick a model, or click 'More models'; changes apply from Claude's next response. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Effort levels in the app are Low, Medium, High, Extra high (Opus 4.7 and newer) and Max; higher effort is more thorough but takes longer and uses more of your limits. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Thinking cannot be turned off on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 or Opus 5; to make Claude think less, choose a lower effort. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Factors that use limits faster include message length, attachment size, conversation length, tool use, model choice, effort level, artifacts and multi-step tasks. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 run safety classifiers on every request and on content the model reads; higher-risk cyber requests may fall back to Opus 4.8 and Opus 5.5 biology dual-use requests fall back to Opus 5. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16049681-why-claude-switched-models-in-your-conversation-with-opus-5-or-opus-5-5]

Claude's Research feature runs on Opus 5.5 and falls back to Opus 4.8 when needed, regardless of the model selected for the chat. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11088861-use-research-on-claude]
Like previous Opus models, Opus 5.5 is available with zero data retention; it is no longer available with thinking switched off. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]
Opus 5.5 is available on all platforms including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure; developers use the model ID claude-opus-5-5. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

Claude can 'hallucinate' incorrect or misleading information; Anthropic says not to rely on it as a single source of truth and to scrutinize high-stakes advice and check cited sources. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8525154-claude-is-providing-incorrect-or-misleading-responses-what-s-going-on]

Claude can hallucinate its own capabilities, such as claiming to have sent emails; it has no access to tools that are not explicitly integrated. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241188-claude-is-producing-links-that-don-t-work-and-falsely-claiming-that-it-has-sent-emails-or-produced-external-documents-what-s-going-on]
Mojeed Abisiga is a data and AI leader and educator whose mission is to make data and AI easy for everyone; he teaches people to use AI at work. [author]

Claude Opus 5 API pricing was $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens; Opus 5.5 is $4/$20, with cache reads at $0.20 per million and batch processing at half price ($2/$10). [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/whats-new-opus-5-5]

On the API, Opus 5.5's default effort is medium, while Opus 5 defaulted to high; adaptive thinking is always on and effort controls thinking depth. Requests that try to switch thinking off return a 400 error, and forced tool use (tool_choice any or tool) is not supported. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/whats-new-opus-5-5]

In Anthropic's testing, Opus 5.5 at medium effort matches or exceeds Opus 5 at high effort on coding and knowledge-work evaluations; at a given level it tends to think more per turn than Opus 5, especially at xhigh and max. Anthropic advises reserving xhigh and max for work where you have measured a quality gain, and lowering effort first to get less thinking, which cuts thinking, cost and latency more reliably than prompt instructions. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-opus-5-5]

Anthropic's docs say Opus 5.5 is much less likely to state an incorrect figure or cite the wrong source, and catches details that are easy to miss in large inputs, such as a date in a long planning thread that falls on the wrong weekday or a chart in a slide deck that doesn't match the underlying figures; its spreadsheets, slides and documents need less editing before you share them. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-opus-5-5]

For long agentic tasks, Anthropic advises treating a text-only end of turn as a report rather than proof the task is done, keeping the task's parts in a checklist, stating the completion condition up front, and stopping after two or three automatic continuations on the same task rather than repeating them indefinitely. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-opus-5-5]

The help centre's effort descriptions: Low and Medium work well for routine tasks and stretch your usage further; High offers the best overall balance of quality and speed; Extra high is designed for long-running coding and agentic tasks, with deeper reasoning than High (Opus 4.7 and newer); Max is the most thorough option, for the deepest reasoning. Each model's recommended level is marked 'Default' in the menu, and you can change model, effort or thinking at any point in a conversation. The thinking toggle doesn't appear for models where thinking is always on. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Further Anthropic-reported Opus 5.5 results: Humanity's Last Exam 67.7% with tools, AutomationBench 40.0%, CursorBench 4.0 57.8%, OSWorld 2.1 81.8% (partial) for computer use, Chartography 89.0% with tools for chart recognition. At default (medium) effort: FrontierCode 54.6%, which Anthropic says beats GPT-6 Astra's top score (53.3%) for about a fifth of the cost per task, and CursorBench 52.5%. On GDPval-AA v2.1, Anthropic's table lists GPT-6 Astra at 1542 and GPT-5.6 Sol at 1588. Unless noted, results use adaptive thinking at max effort with production safeguards on, which Anthropic says likely reduces some scores. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

Fast mode for Opus 5.5 is available in Claude Code and the Claude Platform with up to 2.5x speed, at $8 per million input and $40 per million output tokens. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5]

Claude Fable 5.2 was announced November 9, 2026, generating output up to 30% faster than the 5.1 versions. Fable models are on all paid plans: on Max, Ultra and Team/Enterprise premium seats you can spend up to 50% of weekly limits on them; on Pro and Team standard seats they run on usage credits. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15424964-claude-fable-models-on-your-plan]

Opus 5.5 ships with Fable-class cybersecurity safeguards (routine bug finding and fixing allowed, most cybersecurity tasks re-routed to Opus 4.8) and adds a biology safety classifier; classifiers also screen content the model reads, such as memory, connectors, search results and files. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16049681-why-claude-switched-models-in-your-conversation-with-opus-5-or-opus-5-5]

Anthropic's prompting guidance: treat Claude like a brilliant but new employee who lacks context; be specific about output format and constraints; explicitly give Claude permission to say 'I don't know', which Anthropic says can drastically reduce false information; for long documents, ask for word-for-word quotes first and have each claim backed by a quote or retracted (these reduce but do not eliminate hallucinations). [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices] [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations]

Anthropic's Claude Code guide suggests planning with Opus and executing with Sonnet (built in as /model opusplan). [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14552983-models-usage-and-limits-in-claude-code]

Outside the newest models, Claude's context window is 200K tokens, which Anthropic describes as about 500 pages of text or more. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans]
